title: Throttling and quotas
scenario: Saltmarsh Weather API sells forecast data through a public API whose EC2 backend serves at most 1,500 requests per second, about 15 per vCPU. Ten paid customers are entitled to 100 requests per second each and 100 free-tier developers to 4 each, so contracted traffic can reach 1,400. The company's own web front end calls the same API without a key and once produced a 40-minute retry storm. The recovery Region has 64 vCPUs of compute allowance from the account's initial setting, and its copy of the API has no per-customer limits configured. Partner mobile apps currently retry rejected calls immediately in a tight loop.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
Each paid customer is held to 100 requests per second and each free-tier developer to 4
The backend must never receive more than 1,500 requests per second from any combination of callers, including the company's own front end
After a disaster is declared, no limit may need to be raised before the recovery Region carries the full 1,500 requests per second
requiredArtifact: Architecture decision record + diagram notes + cost assumptions + guidance for API callers on rejected requests

rubric.label: Why live lab was unsuitable documented
Every caller class is held to its stated rate, and total traffic reaching the backend cannot exceed 1,500 requests per second even from the company's own keyless front end
Before any failover, the recovery Region's compute allowance and API rate settings both admit and serve the full 1,500 requests per second

constraint_reason: Service unavailable or not disposable in a personal same-day lab
